Retain the packed 32-bit word until STORE writes it into the low four byte lanes of a 128-bit SRAM line. valid clears only when the write is accepted. object.label: TYPE_q / BANK_q / valid
object.tooltip: Read response tags delayed to match SRAM latency. The destination decoder uses TYPE_q, not the live TYPE for the next request. It generates one selected bank enable on a valid response.

object.label: FIFO_VALID / FULL
object.tooltip: Result-available status to sequencer. POST is blocked while full. STORE consumes one entry after SRAM write acceptance. DONE is issued only after final required write.

object.label: SRAM response timing
object.tooltip: Wrapper-generated timing signal to the sequencer. A memory macro may supply only Q; then the wrapper pipelines RD_EN to form RD_VALID. It does not autonomously choose addresses.

REGISTER UPDATE RULES (on rising clk)
reset: acc <= 0. Else if load_bias: acc <= bias. Else if mac_en: acc <= acc + signextend(product). Else: hold acc.
x_cap / w_cap independently load operand registers from SRAM rdata[7:0]. No accumulator update during operand capture.
The final accumulation edge updates acc; the following POST edge captures the activated / shifted / clamped result.

NUMERIC CONTRACT
Accumulator width is 32 bits, replacing the original diagram's ambiguous 16-bit result path. INT8 output conversion is explicitly included.
ReLU: max(0, acc), or bypass. Then arithmetic right shift (floor division by 2^shift), then clamp to [-128, 127].
This is a simple fixed-point baseline, not general framework-compatible quantization. Per-layer shift is supplied by software.
Arithmetic overflow must be prevented by the supported K / bias range; this model does not saturate the accumulator.
The result completes one neuron's dot product, not necessarily the entire matrix or layer.

TIMING CONTRACT
At a REQ edge, SRAM samples addr/re and updates registered rdata after the edge. At the following CAP edge, the destination captures that stable rdata. No read is issued in CAP. Writes commit at STORE edges. POST follows the final MAC edge; it cannot capture the new final acc on that same edge.

LATENCY / HANDSHAKE
For a full two-neuron pair: 4 bias edges + 7*K operand/compute edges + 1 POST edge + 2 STORE edges = 7*K+7 edges AFTER start acceptance. For K=3: 28 periods from E1 to E29 (29 listed edges including start). This schedule is intentionally unpipelined: only K of those edges perform two MAC updates. done becomes high after E29; hold DONE until ack, then return IDLE. busy=1 during execution and 0 in IDLE / DONE.

NEXT-LAYER HANDOFF
Layer L reads A and writes B. After ALL outputs are stored, the next layer reads B and writes A. Update K_next = N_previous and select the next weights, biases and shift. A and B are separate address regions, not separate SRAM ports. They must each fit their assigned layer activations. This baseline runs one configured layer per start; host reconfigures before the next start.

SCOPE AND LIMITS
This is a cycle-defined architectural specification, not a synthesized or RTL-validated implementation. No AXI, DMA, instruction fetch, SRAM stalls, or overlapping reads/writes are assumed. The Result FIFO block is specified as a depth-1 output hold stage: two simultaneous results (q0, q1 plus valid bits) are captured explicitly, then written separately.
For layers larger than allocated SRAM regions: software must provide tiles and transfers. Preserve 32-bit partial sums across input tiles; apply activation only after the complete dot product. Autonomous tiling / external-memory transfer is not implemented here.
Clock period must satisfy operand register -> multiplier -> 32-bit adder -> accumulator setup, and POST combinational timing. Adding pipeline stages changes the schedule.

REGISTERED TIMING
SRAM Q, W/I/B/CFG bank Q, final accumulator tile, activation tile, requantized tile and FIFO are registered. Newly captured Q is available only next edge. The generic callback order is unchanged: controller, SRAM, demux, W/I/B/CFG banks, MAC array, activation, scale, FIFO. Only control and demux outputs are wires. Every PE reads its own old accumulator; final bias is never added twice.

SRAM / TILE LAYOUT
Line indices: W1=000,W2=001; initial/final=200; hidden=201 only without fusion; B1=300,B2=301; CFG1=380,CFG2=381. W lane r holds W[r,0..3]. I lane v holds fourfeatures for independent vector v; output lane v holds fourneurons. Bias lane r is INT32. CFG lanes=M,S,ReLU,reserved0. Input/result lanes are not replicated. Byte-enable masks preserve inactive vectors.

Single-vector latency is not faster than the uploaded20-cycle model. Four independent vectors now fit the same20-edge run.

SCOPE / CORAL RELATIONSHIP
Uses an outer-product formulation with local INT32 accumulators, consistent with the current Coral matrix-engine concept; not a Coral RTL clone or the earlier diagonal weight-stationary grid. Shadow parameters preload via local AGU reads, not external DMA. Fusion is explicitly scheduled for this known two-layer tile, not a compiler implementation. Up to16 parallel postprocessing paths are assumed. Fixed dimensions, two layers, one128-bit SRAM port, one-cycle response; no synthesized timing claim. See README.md and CYCLE_TRACE.md.

CONTROL / TIMING CONTRACT
Controller issues one SRAM transfer per clock. TYPE and BANK delay with the read response. Prefetch bank1 W/B/CFG at layer1 C1/C2/C3 while bank0 is held stable.
Bank muxes switch only after all W/I/B/CFG loaded flags are visible. Each register capture takes effect for consumers on the following edge. Active-bank writes are rejected.
Input forwarding captures the already-quantized hidden tile; never raw INT32 sums. Layers are sequential because layer2 depends on hidden results. Parameter fetch overlaps compute; dependent layer arithmetic does not.
PE bias/feedback mux selects bias at C1, own old accumulator thereafter. Multiplier8x8, adder/acc32; overflow is a model error. No long combinational neighbour accumulation.

UTILIZATION / SCOPE
Four independent input vectors provide16 useful MACs per compute clock. A single vector enables only4 PEs; batching is not a free single-vector latency reduction.
Default two-layer batch:20 modeled edges,7 SRAM reads,1 finalwrite,3 overlapped parameter reads,1 hidden-tile forward. BATCH4:100% compute-only utilization;40% whole-run.
External DMA, RISC-V execution, compiler/automatic fusion, arbitrary matrix tiling, more than two layers and variable-latency ready/valid are not implemented. This is an architectural C simulator, not an HLS top or a timing-verified RTL design.
Current Coral matrix engine uses an outer-product formulation; this small model borrows the concept rather than reproducing its RTL. See README references.
